title: Chinese Beef and Potato Stew
subtitle: 土豆炖牛肉
creator: 小麗 (教做菜)
ingredients: 500 g beef rib fingers or stewing beef
300 g potatoes, cut into rolling-cut chunks
4 slices ginger, plus 1 smashed piece for blanching
steps: Place the beef in water with one smashed piece of ginger. Bring to a boil over high heat and skim away the foam.
Heat a little oil over low heat. Melt the rock sugar until it becomes deep reddish brown.
Add the drained beef and stir-fry quickly over medium-high heat until coated and browned.
Reduce to medium-low. Add scallion, ginger, star anise, cassia and bay leaves, followed by the cooking wine, light soy sauce and dark soy sauce.
Add the tomatoes and stir-fry over medium-high heat until softened.
Add the dried hawthorn and 1 L boiling water. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce to low and stew for 1 hour 15 minutes. The reel also gives a pressure-cooker option of 15 minutes on low after pressure is reached.
Add the potatoes and continue cooking until tender. The reel marks this later stage as 15 minutes.
Add half a spoonful of salt, cover and finish over medium-low heat. Serve with rice.

The reel gives both ordinary-pot and pressure-cooker timings.
The spoon size for salt is not specified.

title: Cucumber Sandwiches
subtitle: Herbed cream cheese tea sandwiches
creator: Cooking Classy · Jaclyn
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste

Fold in the mayonnaise, chives, parsley, dill, lemon zest, lemon juice and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the cream cheese mixture over one side of every bread slice.
Cover half of the slices generously with cucumber. Top with the remaining bread, spread-side down.
Press lightly, trim the crusts if desired, and cut into halves or quarters. Serve immediately.

title: Korean Braised Chicken
subtitle: Jjimdak · 찜닭
creator: Angela | SF Food & Lifestyle
ingredients: 2 medium white or Yukon Gold potatoes, about 10 oz
3 to 4 mushroom caps, rehydrated dried shiitake or fresh mushrooms
2 to 3 dried whole red chili peppers, or 4 to 5 small ones
1 to 2 fresh chili peppers or jalapeños, optional
2 tbsp oyster sauce, or additional soy sauce
2 tbsp rice wine, mirim or mirin
2 tbsp dark brown sugar, or regular sugar
3 to 4 tbsp corn syrup, rice syrup or oligo syrup, or 2 to 3 tbsp honey
steps: Soak the sweet potato starch noodles in warm water for about 30 minutes, then drain well.
Trim excess fat from the chicken. Cut the potatoes into 1 1/2-inch chunks and soak them in water. Cut the carrot, mushrooms and onion into bite-size pieces.

Place the chicken in a large pot and add 3 cups water. Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine, sugar, syrup or honey, and black pepper. Bring to a boil uncovered over high heat. Boil for about 10 minutes and skim off the foam.
Add the potatoes, carrot, mushrooms, onion, dried chilies, garlic and ginger. Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes.
Gently mix in the fresh chilies, scallions and drained noodles. Cook uncovered for about 3 minutes, until the noodles are tender and glossy.
Stir in the sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot.

title: One-Pan Lemon Chicken Orzo
subtitle: Healthy 30-minute dinner
creator: Mallory Brown, RDN
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 tsp kosher salt (start with 1/4 tsp if using fine table salt), more to taste
2 to 4 tbsp lemon juice (1 to 2 large lemons), start with 2 tbsp
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the olive oil and, once hot, add the onion. Saute 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the chicken, garlic and seasonings, making sure the chicken is coated. Cook 3 to 4 minutes on one side undisturbed, then flip and cook another 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through to 165F (75C).
Add the orzo and broth, stir well, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer on low 12 minutes, stirring occasionally so the orzo does not stick.
Remove the lid and simmer another 2 to 4 minutes until the orzo is cooked; there will still be excess liquid.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts. Turn off the heat and stir in the Greek yogurt, parmesan, lemon juice and zest. Add salt as needed.
Let it sit briefly; the orzo will keep absorbing the remaining liquid as it rests.

title: Chilled Silken Tofu
subtitle: Cold tofu with soy, sesame and scallion

imageCredit: Photo: rhosoi, via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY
ingredients: 1 block silken or soft tofu, kept cold
1 scallion, finely sliced, especially the green parts

A few drops of black vinegar, optional
steps: Chill the tofu and serving plate. Keep the tofu refrigerated until the moment you assemble the dish.
Pour off the water and gently unmold the tofu onto the plate in one careful motion.
Leave the tofu whole or cut it into 3 to 4 clean, thick slices and fan them slightly.
Immediately before serving, drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, then scatter the scallion and sesame seeds over the top.
evidence: Dress the tofu only when it is going to the table. If it sits in soy sauce, it releases water and loses its clean presentation.

title: Steamed Egg Custard
subtitle: Silky, tofu-like Chinese steamed egg
creator: Eric & Lulu
imageCredit: Photo: Tam3415, via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 2.0
ingredients: About 1 cup plus 2 tbsp water or broth, based on the measured egg volume
A few drops of toasted sesame oil, optional
steps: Gently stir the eggs with the salt until fully combined. Do not whip in air.
Measure the beaten eggs, then stir in 1.5 times that volume of water or broth. Three large eggs are about 3/4 cup, so use about 1 cup plus 2 tbsp liquid.
Strain the mixture through a mesh strainer into a heatproof serving bowl. Skim off any surface bubbles.
Cover the bowl with foil or a small plate so condensation cannot pit the surface.
Steam gently over low to medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes. It is done when the center is just set and wobbles like soft gelatin without sloshing.
Remove from the heat and finish with a few drops of sesame oil and sliced scallion greens. Serve warm.
evidence: The recommended ratio is 1 part beaten egg to 1.5 parts liquid for a very soft, silky texture. Use a 1-to-1 ratio for a firmer, more tofu-like custard.
Straining removes stringy egg bits and helps produce a smooth surface.
Gentle heat matters most. High heat creates bubbles, a spongy texture and watery pockets.
Water works well. A little beef broth gives the custard more flavor.

title: Instant Pot Galbi Jjim
subtitle: Korean braised beef short ribs
creator: Esther Soyeon Park Chun
ingredients: 6 lb sliced beef back ribs or beef short ribs
2 tbsp honey, plus more if omitting the pear juice
steps: Rinse the ribs, then soak them in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood.
While the ribs soak, cut the potatoes, carrots, green onions and onion into chunks. Reserve some green onion for garnish.
Mix the water, Korean pear juice, soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, honey and black pepper.
Rinse the soaked ribs thoroughly in cold water. Place them in the Instant Pot and pour the sauce over them.
Cook at high pressure for 35 minutes.
Place the vegetables in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with a plate and microwave for 5 minutes. This keeps them from becoming too soft in the pressure cooker.
When the ribs are done, skim off and discard excess oil from the surface.
Add the partially cooked vegetables to the Instant Pot. Use Saute mode for 10 to 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender to your liking and the sauce has reduced.
Garnish with green onion and sesame seeds, then serve with rice.
For a regular pot, simmer the ribs and sauce covered over low heat for about 1 1/2 hours. Add the vegetables and cook about 30 minutes longer, until tender.
evidence: The creator provides the full ingredient quantities and directions in the reel caption.
The video confirms the main sequence: preparing the vegetables and sauce, rinsing the ribs, pressure cooking, adding the vegetables, and serving the finished galbi jjim with rice.
The caption gives both Instant Pot and regular-pot methods. The pear juice is explicitly optional, with extra honey suggested as a substitute.

title: Sweet Potato Tapioca Balls
subtitle: Taiwanese-style dessert with grass jelly
creator: Lucy Wang
steps: Steam the sweet potato and purple sweet potato until very soft.
Mash the orange and purple potatoes separately with a fork.
Mix 3/4 cup tapioca flour into each cup of mashed potato. Knead each mixture until it forms a cohesive ball.
Divide the dough into manageable pieces and roll them into logs.
Cut the logs into small, evenly sized nuggets.
Bring 4 cups of water to a boil. Add the potato balls and cook until they float to the surface.
Immediately strain the cooked balls and transfer them to an ice bath to preserve their chewy texture.
Assemble the dessert with coffee ice cubes and grass jelly. Add the orange and purple potato balls, then drizzle generously with honey.
